elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "Customer may also assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger/acquisition/sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets."

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "Neither party will assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of the other party"

elements.element: Vendor-side consent standard: not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld" (now applied to consent of "the other party")

elements.element: Vendor never to assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "IBM will not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Customer"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: Clause contains no change-of-control termination right; condition demonstrably absent ("Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void." is the only consequence)

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors (Vendor side included) with written notice
elements.evidence: Successor carve-out runs to Customer only: "Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization"; no notice mechanic

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "without the prior written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are satisfied: the consent requirement now binds IBM (reasonableness standard preserved), Customer retains consent-free assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, an affiliate carve-out is added, and IBM is barred from assigning to a Customer competitor.
The 'no Vendor termination right on change of control' element is conditionally satisfied because the clause creates no such right and none was introduced.

Edits are surgical: one operator change ('Neither party'/'the other party'), one short list addition ('or sale of substantially all assets'), and one concise sentence for the two absent protections; no whole-clause rewrite and no fallback mechanics (written-notice regime) imported.

Untouched terms remain effective: voidness of non-permitted assignments and Customer's continuing liability on permitted assignment are preserved; no undefined terms or dangling mechanics introduced ('competitor of Customer' is used in its ordinary sense).
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no Vendor successor right, no written-notice mechanic), but that is irrelevant since the locked preferred level is complete.
